Meeting header
Date: 2026-04-03 15:00 PT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Marisol Gomez (Redwood SE), Evan Rhodes (LumenBridge Head of ML), Priya Desai (Platform Lead), Mark Chen (CTO)

Auto-generated Summary: Samir kicked off the POC scoping; primary focus is to agree on success criteria (latency, cost per token, availability), define workload sizing and representative prompt set, and schedule benchmarks on Redwood Dedicated. Customer has strict budget runway and needs per-token economics and batching knobs documented.

Topics: success criteria; workload sizing and traffic profile; benchmark plan (datasets, seeds, metrics); cost modeling (per-token, batching, caching); timeline and next steps; security/compliance touchpoints.

Transcript: 
[00:00] Samir (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Samir from Redwood. quick check on audio?
[00:04] Evan (LumenBridge): good here, hey Samir, thanks.
[00:06] Priya: all good.
[00:08] Samir: cool. i'll run real quick through agenda. want to align success criteria for the pilot, get your traffic numbers, agree bench plan and then we'll talk unit economics — per token, batching, caching, that sort of knobs.
[00:21] Mark: yeah, our main ask is can you show us something that maps to dollars per thousand queries, basically how much this costs to run in production. we have a hard runway for budget Q3.
[00:31] Marisol (Redwood SE): great. to set expectations, we'll propose two bench passes — one synthetic at scale to validate throughput, and one representative pass using your prompt set to measure latency and per-token consumption. we'll instrument token counts, GPU utilization, and tail latency.
[00:45] Evan: sounds good. about models — do you recommend hosted or dedicated for the pilot? we worry about both cost and PII controls.
[00:52] Samir: good question. for an econ-focused pilot we usually do Dedicated so you get predictable throughput and accurate unit-econ numbers; hosted can be done but it's noisy for reserved capacity math. Dedicated also makes it easier to toggle quantization profiles and batching rules. there is the VPC/private plane option if you need strict network isolation but that's a separate setup.
[01:12] Priya: we probably need VPC controls in the longer run, but for now dedicated in your managed environment might be fine. can you share what metrics you'll collect during the run?
[01:20] Marisol: yes — tokens in/out, request rate, p50/p90/p99 latencies, GPU type, instances used, batching efficiency, and cache hit ratio if we enable prefix caching. we'll also capture prompt length distribution so the per-token estimate can be normalized.
[01:37] Evan: quick clarifying — prefix caching, is that automatic or something we opt in?
[01:41] Marisol: we can enable automatic prefix/KV caching, but you can control TTL and prefix keys. for a QA workflow it often gives a high hit rate, reduces repeat tokens, and improves cost. but it depends on prompt reuse.
[01:53] Mark: what's the typical improvement?
[01:55] Marisol: varies — we've seen anywhere from 5% to 40% token reduction depending on workload duplication. for chat-style with repeated context it tends to be higher.
[02:05] Evan: on batching, do you control batch sizes automatically? i.e., will you trade latency for cost? we have an SLA to keep p95 under 400ms.
[02:15] Samir: yes, batching is workload-aware. we can set a latency SLO and a max batching window. for this pilot, we can run two configurations: aggressive batching for cost baseline, and latency-constrained batching to measure the tradeoff. that'll give you two per-token cost points.
[02:30] Priya: perfect. for success criteria, can we list concrete numbers? what about p95 latency, availability, and cost per 1k tokens?
[02:38] Samir: proposal: success if p95 < 400ms on representative prompts, 99.5% availability during bench run, and cost per 1k tokens under $X — we'll plug in a baseline after the first synthetic run. is that OK?
[02:50] Evan: yes. i also want unit economics broken down by model variant — e.g., smaller quantized model vs full 16-bit model.
[02:58] Marisol: we'll include model variant comparisons, quantization planes (8-bit, 4-bit if supported), and the delta in throughput/cost. we'll also capture BLEU/ROUGE or task-specific metric if you provide evaluators.
[03:12] Mark: timeline? we need results before end of april to present to finance.
[03:16] Samir: ok, so timeline: you send traffic sample by Apr 10, we provision bench by Apr 11-12, run synthetic bench Apr 13, run representative bench Apr 14-15, analyze and deliver a cost model and report Apr 17. that fits?
[03:30] Priya: tight but doable. we'll prioritize the traffic sample.
[03:34] Evan: regarding cost model assumptions, what inputs do you need from our side?
[03:38] Samir: tokenization and average tokens per prompt, desired concurrency, expected qps distribution over day, and any retention/PKI/KMS needs for encrypt-at-rest. also whether you'll require audit logs and longer retention — that affects storage costs.
[03:52] Evan: for concurrency we typically see bursts up to 300 qps but steady state 50 qps. average prompt ~120 tokens, response ~200 tokens.
[04:00] Marisol: good data point. that will allow us to estimate batching envelope and effective tokens per request. also please share percent of requests that reuse context (e.g., follow-ups) — caching impact depends on that.
[04:12] Evan: roughly 30% follow-ups right now, but we can extract better numbers from logs.
[04:16] Samir: one thing to call out — GPU selection matters a bunch. for high throughput we may recommend A100 equivalent or H100 depending on model. H100 gives better throughput for some FP16/amp kernels but pricing differs. we'll outline cost curves.
[04:32] Mark: will you include a sensitivity analysis for token price vs qps and model choice?
[04:36] Marisol: yes, we'll produce a small table: per-1k-token cost across batch sizes and cache hit rates and then model variant. it's basically a 3-d sensitivity slice but we'll highlight the realistic region for your workload.
[04:48] Evan: any gotchas on warm-start / KV cache blowup? we've seen high memory from long conversations.
[04:53] Marisol: we'll measure KV cache growth during long sessions. for very long contexts we might recommend prefix trimming and fixed windowing. that will be part of the runbook and we'll surface memory per-conversation.
[05:06] Priya: compliance questions — we need SOC 2 related docs and list of sub-processors, plus is SSO integration possible for your console?
[05:13] Samir: yes, we will share SOC2 and a list of infra sub-processors. SSO/SAML is supported for Redwood Console; for Dedicated we'll walk you through the service account model and RBAC. I'll attach security docs to the follow-up email.
[05:26] Evan: on pricing, what's the delta between a pilot discounted rate and normal hosted pricing? we want to model steady-state.
[05:33] Samir: pilots usually have a one-time credit or discounted bench credits. the long-term pricing for Dedicated is usage-based with reserved commits if you want a runway. for the model we will use current published rates as baseline and show the pilot credit as a separate line item.
[05:48] Mark: can we get an example cost breakdown for a week? like 1M requests, given our tokens?
[05:54] Marisol: yes, once we have your prompt distribution and qps curve, we'll produce a sample weekly cost with breakdown by model and batching configuration.
[06:02] Evan: let's talk concrete benchmarks — what dataset should we send?
[06:05] Marisol: ideally a 1-2k sample of real prompts that represent high-, mid-, and low-length cases, and a parallel evaluation set if you want qualitative metrics. also a 7-day anonymized traffic log for qps distribution.
[06:19] Priya: we'll aim to deliver that by Apr 10.
[06:22] Samir: great. any internal approval needs for the pilot? who else needs to be looped in?
[06:27] Mark: finance will want the five-week runbook and the projected cost, security will want SOC2 docs. i'll loop in Lina from finance and Jorge from security after this meeting.
[06:38] Evan: one more question about fallback policies — if capacity is constrained, do you have automatic model fallbacks?
[06:44] Marisol: Redwood supports routing policies and fallbacks so you can route to cheaper quantized model or another region. we'll show how that impacts latency and quality in the report.
[06:54] Samir: ok to recap — action items: Samir sends pricing + template, Marisol sets up bench, LumenBridge sends traffic + prompt set, Priya confirms compliance contacts. we aim to run benches second week of April and deliver report Apr 17.
[07:10] Priya: yep. thanks everyone.
[07:12] Mark: thanks.
[07:14] Evan: thanks.
[07:15] Samir: i'll follow up with a calendar invite and the docs.
